channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: “Tem a mesma cultura golpista do pai”, diz presidente do PT sobre Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The national president of the Workers' Party (PT), Edinho Silva, criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for repeating false claims about Brazil's electronic voting machines being linked to the Venezuelan company Smartmatic, accusing him of having 'the same coupist culture as his father'. He noted these claims have already been refuted by the TSE in previous electoral cycles.

item.title: Renato Casagrande lidera disputa pelo Senado no ES, diz pesquisa
item.description: Former governor Renato Casagrande (PSB) leads the Senate race in Espírito Santo, according to a Real Time Big Data poll released on July 22, 2026, with at least 30% of voter intentions. Paulo Hartung (PSD) and Sérgio Meneguelli (PSD) are tied for second place depending on the scenario. The survey interviewed 1,600 voters between July 20–21, has a 95% confidence level, a 2-point margin of error, and is registered with the TSE under ES-04482/2026.

item.title: Pesquisa mostra empate técnico com Lula e fragilidade oculta de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Real Time Big Data poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro technically tied with Lula in the second round (42% each), but with hidden fragility: 67% of his voters say they would switch to a more competitive alternative, compared to only 33% who would stay loyal. In contrast, 73% of Lula’s voters say they would not change their candidate, indicating a far more solid base. Smaller candidates like Zema (82%) and Caiado (80%) show even higher vote-switching propensity, while Renan Santos has a divided base (55% loyal, 45% unstable).

item.title: Lula sanciona lei que reforça proteção a honorários de advogados
item.description: President Lula signed Law No. 15.472/2024, which strengthens the protection of lawyers' fees by classifying them as privileged credits in bankruptcy, judicial recovery, insolvency, and creditor proceedings. The law establishes that such fees enjoy the same treatment as labor credits and can be enforced directly as an executive title.

item.title: Ministros do TSE veem atuação de campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro para desacreditar pesquisas
item.description: TSE ministers identified the legal campaign of Flávio Bolsonaro working to discredit electoral polls using false data to undermine survey credibility. This follows the same pattern of attacking electronic voting machines, expanding the scope of electoral disinformation. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Flávio “tem mesma cultura golpista” de Jair Bolsonaro, diz PT
item.description: The national president of the Workers' Party (PT), Edinho Silva, accused pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro of sharing the same 'coupist culture' as his father, Jair Bolsonaro, after he questioned the security of Brazil's electronic voting machines in an event with diplomats. Silva likened the remarks to the July 2022 incident that led to Bolsonaro's ineligibility and stated the PT is evaluating legal actions against what it calls an antidemocratic offensive.

item.title: Irmão de Michelle rebate Eduardo Bolsonaro e ironiza falas de ex-deputado
item.description: Eduardo Torres, brother of former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro, countered Eduardo Bolsonaro on social media after the ex-deputy called Michelle's video — in which she expressed disagreements with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and the PL party — 'immature.' Torres mocked Eduardo Bolsonaro's remarks, defending Michelle's stance and accusing him of hypocrisy. The clash reflects growing internal tensions within Bolsonarismo ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Rede pede que STF reconheça responsabilidade por indicação de emendas
item.description: The Sustainability Network filed an action at the STF demanding that lawmakers who impose budget amendments be held accountable like expenditure managers, arguing they wield equivalent power without financial oversight or sanctions for misappropriation. The party claims the lack of transparency turns public funds into tools of personal, territorial, or clientelist power. The move follows rulings by Minister Flávio Dino requiring party transparency on amendments and suspending those allegedly irregularly indicated by Liberal Party president Valdemar Costa Neto.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: O fantasma da fraude eleitoral está de volta
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program discussed Flávio Bolsonaro's warning about potential electoral fraud during a meeting with ambassadors. It also covered the bolsonarist effort to find a running mate for the former president's son. The article was first published on O Antagonista.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro prova que tem mesma cultura golpista de Jair Bolsonaro, diz Edinho Silva
item.description: PT President Edinho Silva stated that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for the 2026 presidency, shares the same coup-oriented culture as his father, Jair Bolsonaro, and employs the same tactics used in the 2022 elections.

item.title: Independiente Medellín x Vasco: onde assistir, horário e escalações
item.description: Vasco da Gama faces Independiente Medellín on Wednesday, the 22nd, at 7:00 PM Brasília time, at Atanasio Girardot in Colombia, in the first leg of the Copa Sudamericana playoffs. The match will be broadcast on ESPN and Disney+, held behind closed doors due to sanctions on the Colombian club for fan invasion during the Libertadores match against Flamengo. Vasco, coming off a loss to Vitória and under new coach Pedro Emanuel, aims to overturn poor Série A form and advance to face Olimpia in the round of 16.

item.title: Presidente do PT diz que Flávio Bolsonaro tem ‘cultura golpista’ do pai e promete ir à Justiça
item.description: The national president of the Workers' Party (PT), Edinho Silva, accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) of sharing the 'coup culture' of his father, Jair Bolsonaro, after meeting with international diplomats to question the reliability of Brazil's electronic voting machines, stating the PT will take the matter to court. He noted that such actions echo Jair Bolsonaro's 2022 statements, which led to his first ineligibility conviction. Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign attempted to counter criticism with a note affirming confidence in the electoral system.

item.title: Maierovitch: Flávio Bolsonaro pode ser cassado se continuar a atacar urnas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) risks having his candidacy registration annulled by the Electoral Justice if he continues spreading false information about electronic voting machines, warned Wálter Maierovitch on UOL News. The warning aims to curb disinformation that undermines public trust in Brazil's electoral system.

item.title: Espere sentado uma condenação do governo Lula ao golpista Ortega
item.description: The text argues that Latin American left-wing politics is intrinsically coup-prone, citing Daniel Ortega and Nicolás Maduro as examples of leaders who abolished elections and jailed opponents. It highlights that Brazilian President Lula was a fraternal ally of these regimes, having compared Ortega to democratic leaders like Angela Merkel in 2021. The central claim is that the left values democracy only as a strategic tool, not as a universal principle.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio reconhece preocupação com fala sobre urnas, mas tenta afastar risco jurídico e traça diferença com caso Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign acknowledges that his remarks on electronic voting machines caused concern and wear, but seeks to minimize legal risk by emphasizing differences with the case that led to Jair Bolsonaro's ineligibility. The team argues the speech occurred at a private event without state apparatus, and that Flávio did not question the integrity of Brazil's electoral system, only citing public facts. The strategy is to avoid equating the episode with the former president's TSE conviction.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Flávio cita dado falso sobre urna eletrônica em meio a obstáculos em articulações
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro made false claims about Brazilian electronic voting machines during a meeting with foreign diplomats, alleging ties to Smartmatic and fraud in Venezuela, despite these assertions having been debunked by Brazil’s Electoral Justice since 2017 and supported by CIA and New York Times reports. Although his pre-campaign denied he questioned the integrity of the electoral system, the incident reinforces his alignment with his father Jair Bolsonaro’s narrative and highlights his struggles to build partisan alliances, secure funding, and gain media traction for a potential 2026 candidacy.

item.title: Lula “cavou esse pênalti”, diz Flávio após início do tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) blamed President Lula (PT) for the new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products, stating that 'Lula dug this penalty'. He pledged to continue working to reverse the measure in a social media post.

item.title: Lula reage a tarifaço em 3 frentes para faturar politicamente
item.description: President Lula's government responds to the 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods with a three-pronged strategy: launching the PT's 'Brazil Will Not Surrender' communication campaign, framing the conflict around U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to link him to Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy, and exercising economic caution by delaying retaliation. The narrative accuses the opposition of supporting U.S. sanctions and portrays Rubio as actively working for Bolsonaro's victory, while Lula avoids direct confrontation with Trump. The approach aims to turn the trade dispute into political capital for reelection by emphasizing job protection, national sovereignty over strategic resources like rare earths, and defense of the Pix system.

item.title: Ao mentir sobre urnas diante de diplomatas, Flávio reacende debate que tornou Bolsonaro inelegível
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) repeated unfounded claims about Brazilian electronic voting machines before foreign diplomats, linking them to the Venezuelan company Smartmatic, already debunked by the TSE. His remarks reignited the debate that led to his father Jair Bolsonaro's ineligibility for using ambassador meetings to spread unverified accusations against the electoral system. While denying he questioned the electoral process, Flávio advocated for greater international election observation, sustaining the narrative of distrust.

item.title: Presidente do PT cita 'cultura golpista' de Flávio e Jair Bolsonaro e diz que não se pode tolerar ataques ao processo eleitoral
item.description: PT president Edinho Silva accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of adopting a 'coup culture' similar to his father Jair Bolsonaro by spreading unfounded doubts about Brazil's electronic voting machines at an international event. Flávio claimed many voting machines used in Brazil are from a company tied to Venezuela's Smartmatic, linking them to alleged fraud in Venezuela and under U.S. investigation, despite the TSE repeatedly stating that Smartmatic does not supply voting machines or software for Brazilian elections.

item.title: “O Brasil Não Se Entrega”: PT lança campanha nacional em resposta a tarifas dos EUA
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) launched the national campaign 'Brazil Will Not Surrender' in response to new U.S. import tariffs, defending national sovereignty, jobs, the economy, and strategic assets like PIX and rare earths. The initiative frames the Lula government as a shield against foreign and domestic pressures, mobilizing the lulista base through digital platforms and spokespeople ahead of the 2026 re-election bid.

item.title: Em resposta ao tarifaço de Trump, PT lança campanha em defesa da soberania
item.description: The PT launched the campaign 'O Brasil Não se Entrega' in response to the 25% tariffs imposed by Donald Trump on Brazilian exports to the U.S., accusing the Bolsonaro family of encouraging such measures against national sovereignty. The initiative includes videos, graphics, and social media mobilization to defend Pix, national industry, and the right of the Brazilian people to determine their own future.

item.title: TSE desmente Flávio Bolsonaro sobre urnas com mesmo texto que contestou o pai em 2022
item.description: The TSE reiterated its 2022 denial, stating that Brazilian electronic voting machines have no connection to the Venezuelan company Smartmatic, contrary to claims by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The tribunal reissued the same statement previously used to counter misinformation about the electoral system.

item.title: Cúpula do PL vê inelegibilidade de Eduardo Bolsonaro como irreversível, mas pode levar suplência ao Senado até setembro
item.description: The PL leadership views Eduardo Bolsonaro's ineligibility as irreversible following his STF conviction, yet retains him as a Senate substitute candidate for André do Prado in São Paulo until September, awaiting final judgment or his voluntary resignation. The party is seeking a replacement, but the final decision rests with Eduardo, who resides in the U.S. and has not participated in proceedings. The PL convention is set for January 25, with substitutions allowed until September 13.

item.title: As notas de Flávio para negar que tenha questionado o sistema de votação
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) issued two official statements denying that he questioned Brazil’s voting system during an event with foreign diplomats in Brasília. The most recent note, co-signed by Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) and legal campaign coordinator Maria Cláudia Bucchianeri, claims he only made technical observations and did not challenge the legitimacy of the electoral process.

item.title: Lula deve manter subsídio da gasolina e gera problema para Fazenda
item.description: President Lula has decided to maintain the R$ 0.44 per liter gasoline subsidy, blocking Finance Minister Dario Durigan’s plan to eliminate it as announced in July. The subsidy, set to expire on July 25, had an initial estimated cost of R$ 2.4 billion for two months, but extending it through December could add R$ 6.3 billion, totaling R$ 8.7 billion in 2026. The move reflects political concerns over inflation and the 2026 elections, despite domestic gasoline prices at Petrobras being significantly below import parity.

item.title: Smartmatic: o que é a empresa venezuelana citada por Flávio Bolsonaro e qual é a relação dela com o Brasil
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro claimed at a diplomatic event that Brazilian electronic voting machines share the same origin as those of Venezuelan company Smartmatic, a claim previously debunked by the TSE, which stated Smartmatic never supplied voting machines or software for Brazilian elections. Although Smartmatic participated in the 2020 bidding process, it lost to Positivo, and the TSE emphasizes that Brazil’s electoral system is entirely designed and managed by the country’s Electoral Justice.

item.title: Lula é desaprovado por 50% e aprovado por 43%, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Gerp poll released on July 22, 2026 shows 50% of respondents disapprove of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government, while 43% approve. Government evaluation indicates 34% rate the administration as 'excellent/good', 23% as 'fair', and 41% as 'bad/terrible'. The survey interviewed 2,000 people between July 15–17, 2026, with a 95% confidence level and is registered with the TSE under BR-05026/2026.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vem fazendo exatamente o que Lula e o PT espera dele
item.description: By repeating the false claim about Venezuelan-made electronic voting machines during a meeting with foreign ambassadors, Flávio Bolsonaro undermined his self-portrayal as a moderate and handed Lula and the PT exactly what they hoped for: a divisive figure who revives the specter of Bolsonarism. His candidacy has become an indirect tool of the PT’s strategy, weakening the right and shielding Lula from backlash over his government’s declining popularity.

item.title: Um dos mais fieis assessores de Lula deixa o Planalto e aterrissa na campanha
item.description: Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola and Chief of Lula's Personal Cabinet, left his position in the Planalto after serving since the start of the government to join the president's reelection campaign, working alongside Gilberto Carvalho on the agenda, as he did in 2022. He will be replaced by his deputy, Oswaldo Malatesta. The information is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Lula é rejeitado por 47% e Flávio, por 46%, diz pesquisa
item.description: Lula is rejected by 47% and Flávio Bolsonaro by 46%, according to a Gerp poll released on July 22, 2026. The survey, conducted among 2,000 respondents between July 15 and 17, has a 95% confidence level and is registered with the TSE under BR-05026/2026. The stimulated poll asked respondents which candidates they would never vote for.

item.title: Sem provas, Flávio Bolsonaro ataca sistema eleitoral com boatos antigos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro repeated unfounded allegations against Brazil’s electoral system, claiming electronic voting machines were made by the Venezuelan company Smartmatic and linked to alleged fraud cited by the CIA, despite the Electoral Justice having debunked these claims for six years. His speech occurred exactly two years after his father Jair Bolsonaro’s similar address at the Alvorada Palace, which led to his ineligibility until 2030 and subsequent conviction for attempting a coup. Flávio’s actions represent a deliberate repetition of the Bolsonaro family’s strategy to delegitimize elections without presenting evidence.

item.title: Flávio e Lula têm empate técnico no 2º turno, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Gerp poll released on July 22, 2026 shows a technical tie between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in a hypothetical 2026 presidential runoff, with 46% and 45% voting intentions respectively, within a 2.19-point margin of error. The survey interviewed 2,000 people from July 15–17, with 95% confidence level and TSE registration BR-05026/2026. Both candidates exhibit high rejection rates: 47% for Lula and 46% for Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Uma má notícia para Paulo Pimenta
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas poll shows petista Paulo Pimenta in fourth place in the Rio Grande do Sul Senate race with 23.7% voting intentions. As Lula's government leader in the Chamber of Deputies and former Secom minister, he trails behind other candidates, signaling a setback for his campaign.

item.title: Juliana Brizola é rejeitada por 27,3% dos eleitores no RS
item.description: Juliana Brizola (PDT) is the most rejected candidate in Rio Grande do Sul for the 2026 elections, with 27.3% of voters stating they would not vote for her, according to a Paraná Pesquisas survey conducted between July 16 and 19, 2026. Federal Deputy Luciano Zucco (PL) ranks second in rejection. The poll, with a margin of error of 2.6 percentage points and 95% confidence level, was funded by the Liberal Party and registered with the TSE under RS-09313/2026.

item.title: Em nova nota, Flávio reafirma 'integral confiança' no sistema eleitoral, mas não explica menção a dado falso sobre urnas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro reaffirmed his 'full confidence' in Brazil's electoral system in a new statement, but did not explain the origin of the false claim linking electronic voting machines to the Venezuelan company Smartmatic, which has been debunked by the TSE since 2017. The statement, signed by him and his pre-campaign team, claims his remarks to foreign diplomats were limited to referencing the meeting that made his father ineligible and a recent CIA report on alleged fraud in Venezuela’s elections, denying he questioned Brazil’s voting system.

item.title: Um plano de governo para o eleitor do Bolsonaro raiz
item.description: Renan Santos of the Missão party unveiled a detailed government plan as a campaign differentiator, emphasizing fiscal reforms, deep changes to the federal pact, and a strict security policy — rare among Brazilian candidates often rely on generic slogans. The documentaing fiscal reforms, federal pact changes, and a strict security agenda — uncommon among Brazilian presidential candidates who typically rely on vague slogans. The proposal targets the core Bolsonaro electorate with concrete, structural measures. O Antagonista highlighted the move as a bold step in the 2026 electoral landscape.

item.title: Palmeiras encara o Coritiba sem Flaco López e Vitor Roque; veja odds
item.description: Palmeiras faces Coritiba away in the 19th round of the Brasileirão without strikers Flaco López and Vitor Roque, who are unavailable due to international duty and post-surgery recovery. Abel Ferreira relies on Ramón Sosa and Jhon Arias to score, as the Verdão leads the league with 41 points and remains favored despite playing away. Odds show 1.85 for a Palmeiras win, 3.40 for a draw, and 4.33 for Coritiba.

item.title: Agenda de Lula: leia os compromissos do presidente nesta 4ª feira
item.description: President Lula spends the day at the Palácio do Planalto focused on economic agenda, including a meeting with the Civil House, a meeting with Stellantis global and regional executives to discuss the automotive sector, and the signing of Bill of Conversion No. 7/2026, which allocates resources to the Brasil Soberano credit program. The agenda includes the presence of Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and government ministers.

item.title: Governo Lula: leia a agenda de ministros nesta 4ª feira
item.description: On Wednesday (July 22, 2026), the Lula government's agenda focuses on the automotive sector, international diplomacy, and culture. Ministers from the Civil House, Development, and Finance are meeting with Stellantis executives at the Planalto Palace, while Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira attends the 3rd Brazil-ASEAN Trilateral Meeting in Manila, and Culture Minister Margareth Menezes attends the Flip literary festival in Paraty. Out of 38 ministers, only 6 had their schedules disclosed.

item.title: Saiba quais são as pesquisas que saem nesta 4ª feira
item.description: New electoral studies registered with the TSE are cleared for publication starting Wednesday, July 22, 2026, covering national surveys and voting intentions in seven Brazilian states: Espírito Santo, Maranhão, Mato Grosso do Sul, Paraná, Piauí, Rio Grande do Norte, and Rio Grande do Sul. The polls may only be released after meeting the legal minimum waiting period and upon registration with the Electoral Justice. Poder360 offers a Poll Aggregator for Drive subscribers, providing access to thousands of surveys since 2000.

item.title: PSB deve sugerir tarifa zero no transporte público para plano de governo de Lula
item.description: The PSB, the party of Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, is expected to propose the inclusion of free public transportation in major cities within Lula’s government plan for a potential fourth term. The suggestion comes from the João Mangabeira Foundation, the PSB’s political training arm, which is participating in discussions over the PT’s program. The measure aims to expand urban transit access and reduce costs for the population.

item.title: E Dudu, hein?
item.description: A survey of 300 readers shows that 53.3% believe Eduardo Bolsonaro should stay in the United States permanently, while 41.7% think he should return to Brazil to be arrested. Only 5% suggest he should do what's best for his father, Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Para 51%, governo Lula é melhor que o de Bolsonaro, diz PoderData
item.description: 51% of Brazilians consider President Lula's government better than Bolsonaro's, according to a PoderData survey from July 2026, showing a 10-point increase over two months. The share viewing Lula's administration as worse dropped to 34%, with 8% seeing them as equal and 6% undecided. The Northeast shows the highest approval (63%), and among low-income earners (up to 2 minimum wages), 56% view the petista government as better.

item.title: PoderData: após tarifaço, aprovação pessoal de Lula vai a 46%
item.description: Following the tariff increase, President Lula's personal approval rose to 46%, tying with 47% disapproval, according to PoderData's July 2026 survey. Government approval also improved slightly to 43% (from 42%), while disapproval remained stable at 51%, signaling a break from months of negative trends. The poll surveyed 2,500 respondents nationwide via landline and mobile calls, with a 2-point margin of error at 95% confidence.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro pode ter que se contentar com uma vice que era o seu plano C
item.description: The PL convention that will confirm Flávio Bolsonaro as the party's 2026 presidential candidate still lacks confirmation of attendance from allied party leaders such as Marcos Pereira (Republicans), Antonio Rueda (Union Brazil) and Ciro Nogueira (PP), indicating weak political coordination. The article suggests Flávio’s original plan may be collapsing, potentially forcing him to accept a 'plan C' vice-presidential pick. The content is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Tarifaço de Trump joga água no chope da convenção de Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faced an unexpected setback just days before the convention that would formalize his 2026 presidential candidacy, following Donald Trump’s announcement of new trade tariffs that triggered economic instability and undermined his campaign’s optimistic outlook. The tariff measures disrupted the favorable economic conditions he had hoped to secure by mid-semester, creating pressure on his narrative of growth and stability. What was meant to be a triumphant convention now unfolds under a cloud of economic uncertainty and doubts about his ability to manage external shocks.

item.title: Tarifaço repercute de forma diferente no Instagram, X e WhatsApp
item.description: The 25% additional tariff imposed by the United States on part of Brazilian exports took effect today, triggering varied reactions across social media: on Instagram, visual content highlights affected producers; on X, the debate is more polarized with accusations of protectionism; on WhatsApp, alarmist messages circulated about job impacts and consumer costs.

item.title: Onde Lula e Flávio enfrentam maiores problemas nos palanques estaduais
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are struggling to form alliances in key states such as Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais, where local parties resist unified slates. Party conventions reveal weaknesses in national coordination, with disagreements over majoritarian candidacies and disputes over ticket placements.

item.title: Tarcísio avalia não ir à convenção do PSD após Kassab publicar montagem do governador com Caiado
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas is considering not attending the PSD convention in person after a post by Gilberto Kassab associated him with Ronaldo Caiado, a rival of his supported candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. The move aims to avoid being photographed alongside Caiado, which could generate campaign material for the Goiás candidate and mislead voters about an alleged alignment. Tarcísio may participate remotely or via a pre-recorded video, maintaining only the state-level PSD endorsement for his re-election.
